page.layout: One page of running text, full width. Running head at the top centre. Signature mark and catchword at the foot. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: in pluribus Christum inveniamus & regnum Christi, non censeri debet à scopo generali scripturarum alienum, cùm testimonium Jesu sit spiritus prophetiæ Apoc. 19: 10. Ille sanè spectandus est ut centrum prophetiæ Act. 10: 43. Hoc proprium fuit Prophetis inquirere in quod & quale tempus inciderent[?] Christi passiones & gloria, 1 Petr. 1: 10. Hinc omnes dicuntur de ipso locuti Luc. 24: 25-27. Act. 3: 18. 24. sicut etiam de diebus restaurationis omnium Act. 3: 19-21. Secuti sumus hac in parte monitum Augustini, qui tract. 9. in Joh. in hunc modum scribit. Lege libros Propheticos, non intellecto Christo; quid tam insipidum & fatuum invenies? intellige ibi Christum, non solùm sapit quod legis, sed etiam inebriat. Christi cognitio procul dubio est clavis cognitionis, & Christi testimonium prima ratio conscribendarum prophetiarum. Quòd si igitur loca de Christo & regno Christi accepta vocabulorum potestatem ita observent, ut in istâ expositione summam & nativam suam emphasin exerceant: atque per analysin eum tueri in cohærentiâ rerum pertractatarum locum cernantur, quem sapiens ordinis dispositio flagitat: ac tandem omnia sic proposita, & eum in modum intellecta scopum ex justâ scribendi occasione deprompta gloriosè exhauriant? dubitandum non puto, quin agnoscenda sint, ut ex mente Dei accepta. Verùm, ut pertinaciæ occurramus, videndum, quid ad demonstrationem hermeneuticam quis tantùm postulare queat, ut rationi cedens in applicatione Prophetiæ ad ejus implementum planè acquiescat? & quid ad eam rem à nobis collatum sit?

p.i: Ad demonstrationem in subjectâ materiâ absolvendam, quam hac nostrâ[?] methodo molimur, nil aliud requiri, quàm solidam probationem consensûs inter ve-

page.notes: Dark ink blotches obscure parts of the line "quod & quale tempus inciderent" (read as "inciderent", uncertain) and the words between "hac" and "nostrâ" in the last paragraph (read as "nostrâ", uncertain). The catchword "rani" at the lower right is partly hard to read and is given with [?]. Printed "dubitandem" in the scan is read as "dubitandum" with the letter uncertain; the printed form may be a typo and is left as printed in the text. The italic boundaries in the body are approximate: the whole Latin body appears to be set in italic, with roman for Scripture references, names and some abbreviations. The end of the last line is a printed hyphen ("ve-") and the paragraph continues on the next page.
